LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Farm.Config: Pick the crop, then zone the whole coverage or paint tiles within it. The machine auto-tills and sows.
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Farm.StepNe: Pick a crop in step ① first - zones need a crop
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Farm.Spec.C: The square working area centred on the machine: auto-tilling, sowing, harvesting and growth driving all happen here. Highlighted when the machine is selected.
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Farm.Spec.F: Barren natural ground inside growing zones is enriched into rich soil (target terrain can be changed via the "renovate terrain" gizmo). Player-built floors are never altered; the original ground is restored whenever the machine is uninstalled, destroyed or moved.
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Farm.Spec.C: Dropped products of the current crop inside growing zones are pulled into the built-in storage (with a converging animation). Only the currently selected crop's product is collected - nothing else.
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Farm.Spec.S: Harvested goods go into the built-in storage first and can be piped to any storage via "set output target"; once full they drop to the ground for haulers or conveyor belts.
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Farm.Spec.P: Built-in solar panels generate during daytime to offset part of the draw (output is always below draw, zero at night); the difference comes from the grid or the backup battery. The machine is also a power conduit node.
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Farm.Spec.B: Charges while on the grid and discharges during blackouts. Same mechanism as vanilla batteries: a fully charged battery may short-circuit in rain or fire - keep it roofed.
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Farm.NeedPo: No power: lay a power conduit adjacent to auto-connect
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Farm.NoGrid: Not on a grid: lay a power conduit adjacent
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Farm.PowerS: Grid output below this machine's draw: build more generators
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Farm.CropHi: Hover a crop to see its stats and description here
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Farm.Terrai: Pick the terrain the machine converts growing-zone tiles into. Third-party terrain mods are supported. It can be changed any number of times: after each change the conversion re-spreads outward from the machine. Removing the machine restores the original terrain (tiles you laid afterwards are kept).
Hover a terrain to see its stats and description here
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Farm.Storag: Drop everything stored in the internal buffer beside the machine for haulers or conveyor belts.
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Zone.Worksh: Designate a workshop zone. Automated processors and conveyor segments placed inside will belong to this workshop.
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Zone.Manage: Open the workshop panel: review its size, free floor space and device list.
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.Devices: Place a processor inside the zone and it will show up here
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.DeviceR: Click the device name to rename it (shown in vanilla UI too)
Leave empty to restore the default name "{0}". Names must be unique among workshop devices on this map.
Another device already has this name: {0}
Another device already has this name, pick a different one
This device is not tracked by any workshop; cannot rename
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.ColActi: Idling… (no station this shift, recreation arranged)
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.PostsNe: ⚠ No workshop type yet: members will only stand duty. Pick a type on the "Settings" tab (press Refresh, then scroll up) and enable vanilla "Manual priorities".
"Planned - no takeover yet" on the right only means this post may not take over (disable) your vanilla work; it does not affect whether a member can work.
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.Pattern: (auto-creates {0} crews and rotates all members in, when this workshop has none)
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.Members: Press "Add member" to assign colonists to this workshop
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.Schedul: Assign shifts from the member list; pawns clock out automatically when a shift ends
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.CrewEmp: Press "Add crew" to create A/B/C/D-named crews, or use "Preset shifts" to lay out two/three shifts and auto-assign members
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.CrewShi: Checked = this crew is responsible for the shift, so crew members join its candidate pool. Unchecked = removed from that shift's candidate pool (on-duty members are unaffected).
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.CrewNoS: No shifts yet; add via "Preset shifts"
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.PerfNoD: Add crews and shifts; on-duty production will be tracked here as daily attendance and output rates
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.ChartNo: Rosters repeat daily; coverage does not change per date (rotations only swap who is on duty)
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.ChartEm: {0} hours are uncovered - use "Apply shift pattern" for two/three-shift rosters
No roster yet. Apply a shift pattern (two/three shifts) or add a crew manually
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.CrewHin: Click a crew header to add members, clear or delete
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.ExcHint: Click a cell to cycle: normal -> leave -> cover
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.Handove: Not in a shift window right now
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.Headcou: How many people this shift puts on duty. Stepping down past zero means "unlimited" - every eligible pawn on that shift will be put on duty, which is usually not what you want. When unset it falls back to 1 person per shift, so a three-shift rotation does not collapse into everyone working every shift.
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.TimeAll: Start = End means an "all-day shift": it covers every hour 0-23, so anyone it picks up will never clock off (and will never go back to bed). To staff a night shift only, set a range such as 20:00 - 08:00.
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.ShiftTa: Click a row to view or edit; the Delete button removes the shift.
Use "Add shift" above, or "Preset shifts" to lay out 2-3 shifts at once.
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.ShiftDe: Delete shift "{0}"? Crews assigned to it will be unassigned.
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.WorkPri: Work priorities: manual - workshop jobs at top priority
Work priorities: simple mode - workshop boost inactive
Vanilla reads priorities only in "manual priorities" mode. With it on, workshop jobs go to top priority (1) so colonists do them first; adjust anytime in the vanilla Work tab.
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.Schedul: Assign members on the Members page first, then press "Add shift" or "Add rotation"
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.TaskSyn: Auto-enables matching Work tab entries (priorities unchanged)
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.ShiftMe: Each meal is a single time of day (e.g. 07:00); once set it is written into the members' timetables
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.FitUnsp: This process declares no expected devices (no native anchor yet)
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.Overvie: Place workbenches (vanilla production benches) or this mod's automated devices inside the workshop zone to wire them in automatically.
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.Setting: Workshop settings open once the device system lands
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.FooterH: {0} device(s) · counted once on open, press Refresh after changes
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Port.BindDe: Click, then pick a target on the map: click a storage cell (any storage - stockpiles, shelves, modded storage included) to output onto that exact cell; click one of this mod's storage machines to feed it directly. One target at a time.
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Port.Unbind: Remove the current output binding. The port stops sending.
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Port.Inspec: Output port: no target bound (use "Set output target…")
No pipe: lay pipe next to this machine
Pipe doesn't reach target: lay pipe adjacent to it
Port idle: needs power, fuel, switch on
Port standing by: goods flow once produced
Target rejects or is full of {0}: adjust filter or free space (port paused)
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Pipe.Alread: There is already a logistics pipe on this tile
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Pipe.Condui: Tile already has a conduit or power transmitter - can't stack
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Pipe.Decons: Deconstruct logistics pipes (including hidden ones). While this designator is active, every pipe segment on the map is highlighted in gold - hidden pipes included. Click or drag to mark for removal.
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Pipe.Inspec: Destination lost: cargo stranded - deconstruct this segment to recover it
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Port.BindRe: Can't bind "{0}": it's not storage that accepts items. Click a stockpile/storage cell, a shelf, or one of this mod's storage machines.
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Port.Manage: Open the logistics panel: set or clear the output target, adjust the output threshold (batch shipping).
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.Overvie: The zone was deleted or the scan has not finished — close and reopen this window
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.Occupan: No cells yet — draw the workshop area first
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.CrewNoM: Empty — open the card to add members
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.ShiftNo: ⚠ No one is available for this shift — assign a crew to it in the Crew settings
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.ChipCli: Click to choose the shift this crew covers
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.CrewNoS: No shifts in this workshop yet — add one in the Shifts tab
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.Confirm: Delete crew "{0}"?\nIts members and shift assignments will be lost. This cannot be undone.
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.Members: hover the card footer for full member details
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.WorkSyn: After you schedule or assign colonists, workshop-related work is raised to top priority (1) so they do workshop jobs first; every other work type keeps the priority you set. "Skipped" counts colonists with work types disabled by vanilla (missing skills or background restrictions).
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.PostsNo: Posts use vanilla work matching the workshop type. Production staff execute bills and briefly await work; other staff use their vanilla services. Meal breaks, rest and shift end follow the timetable.
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.PostDel: This post is declared "self-delivered": the workshop has the matching work type implemented, so "Take over vanilla work" will uncheck it for members.
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.PostNot: This post is not declared "self-delivered" yet: no matching work type is implemented, so it takes no part in takeover (your vanilla work tab is untouched) and it does not affect whether pawns can work - the post table only suggests assignments. "Nothing take-overable" on the Settings page means every post is in this state.
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.PostLan: Writes each post's work type into its holder's vanilla work priorities: ticks it and raises it by skill. Only that one work type per post is touched; nothing else is changed. It never clears or takes over - the "no takeover yet" tag refers to PC delivering its own job, which is a separate matter.
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.Takeove: ON by default: members stop ticking workshop-type vanilla work once assigned (hauling / cleaning / doctor / firefighting unaffected).
Unticks workshop-type vanilla work for members so they focus on the workshop. Release anytime.
Restores only entries the mod took over and you have not changed back.

Heads up: everyone is in a workshop, no free worker left. Hauling / cleaning / doctor / firefighting are always kept by the hard red line, so nobody becomes unusable - but consider keeping one hand free.
not applied: this workshop has no crew members

nothing take-overable: every post is still "Planned - no takeover yet" - the workshop declares no self-delivered work type (this build only implements on-duty jobs, no production jobs). This does not affect whether pawns work: the post table only suggests assignments and never edits your vanilla work tab.
not applied: none of those work types are currently ticked
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.RestPol: Warning: this policy rewrites the work schedule by the daily rotation, so a worker's work hours flip by about 12 hours from day to day and their sleep period shifts violently. Only use it for comparison.
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.LedNoDe: No devices in this zone yet - each device lights up here once placed.
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.Bottlen: Device load (share of accumulated run time)
No run data yet - sampling starts after a second of operation.
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.TrendNo: No output recorded yet - the trend appears once devices here produce.
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.PeakNoD: No run samples yet - hourly totals begin once devices run.
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.PeakFoo: Columns = hour (0-23) - rows = days (oldest on top)
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.EffNoDa: No run records yet - the 7-day comparison appears once devices run.
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.BottleT: No run samples yet - daily totals begin once devices run.
LanguageData.PersonalChronicle.Automation.Tab.HourPic: This meal is scheduled at {0} (only takes effect inside the shift's hours)
Each post stays on one shift for good - no daily flip, so sleep keeps a stable rhythm.
Does not touch the vanilla schedule at all: workers rest when they need to, and duty jobs set the hours.
Old behaviour: the schedule follows whichever shift the crew is on that day.
Warning: rotating daily flips each worker's work hours by about 12 hours from day to day, which wrecks their sleep rhythm.
